question.text: A rifleman is firing at a distant target and has only $10 \%$ chance of hitting it. The least number of rounds he must fire to have more than $50 \%$ chance of hitting it at least once, is

solution.text:
Hint: 
$\mathrm{P}$ (hitting a target) $=\frac{1}{10}$
$\therefore \mathrm{P}($ not hitting a target $)=\frac{9}{10}$
$\therefore$ Let number of trials $=n$
So, $\mathrm{P}($ hitting at least once $)=1-\mathrm{P}$ (missing all) $=1-\left(\frac{9}{10}\right)^{n} \geq \frac{1}{2}$
$\Rightarrow(0.9)^{n} \leq 0.5$
$(0.9)^{6}=0.531441,(0.9)^{7}=0.4782969 \Rightarrow \mathrm{n}=7$
